_comment: Machine config for one photo owner. The engine reads ONLY this file in Phase A; the rest of the pack is Phase C/D. Copy this template, do not edit it in place.
_language_comment: Names the buckets the engine generates (screenshots / to-be-checked / others / AI-images). Confirm it with the owner — photo_census.py reports what the filenames suggest, but a script is not a locale.
_own_camera_makes_comment: EXIF Make values for the OWNER's own devices, from photo_census.py on the first scanned dump. A make left off this list gets its photos described as somebody else's.
_screen_dims_comment: The owner's own screen size(s), each PAIRED with the device it belongs to (G-1): [{"model": "samsung SM-N9750", "dims": [1080, 2280]}]. A no-camera still at exactly that size is a screenshot, in either orientation. The older unpaired shape [[1080, 2280]] is still read, so no existing pack has to be migrated — but an unpaired size cannot be audited ("whose phone was that?") or re-proposed per device. LEAVE THE KEY OUT to keep the engine's built-in iPhone fallback; an empty list turns size-based detection off. Take values from photo_census.py and never from a phone-spec table: 1080x1920 is also the commonest video resolution there is, and accepting it once would have moved 326 ordinary videos.
_declined_screen_dims_comment: Sizes the owner answered `no` to at onboarding ([[1054, 1080]]), written by `photo_onboard_page.py apply --write-pack`. A declined size is never offered as a screen size again and never sends a file to the to-be-checked bucket. Remove a row to be asked again.
_home_locations_comment: Each home carries a fixed id (home-01, home-02, ...) that an index uses instead of the coordinate or the label. It is written by `photo_onboard_page.py apply --write-pack`, or by `photo_onboard_page.py backfill-ids <pack>` for a row typed by hand — never invent one. home_locations_next_id (written with the first id, never by this template) is the next number to issue, so a deleted home's id is never given to another. Suppression reads the coordinate alone and never the id.
_name_budget_comment: N-2's folder-name budget is DELIBERATELY ABSENT here, and adding it to this template would be wrong twice. The SPEC's 20 hard / 12 soft are what photo_profile.name_budget() returns with no key present, so restating them in every new pack makes two copies of one number -- and a benchmark pack must be a blank sheet, which pack_state.assert_blank_sheet checks by finding `naming_spec` empty. To use different numbers, add "name_budget": {"hard": 24, "soft": 14} inside naming_spec below. It counts [who]+[what] only; [period] and [where] are fixed cost. Full-width script counts per character, narrow script per word.
_away_km_comment: away_km is how far from a registered home is still 'home'. It ships at the engine's own 3 km, which is a value and not a guess: measured on a 990-file dump, 60 km typed 11 days spent 1.4-57 km away as everyday life and collapsed 27 natural batches into 17. ⛔ Because this key is WRITTEN here, its presence can no longer show that anybody chose it -- so when the owner answers the onboarding question, write their number AND set away_km_answered to true. Leave the flag false and the run says out loud that its home range was never examined.
